title: First saxophonists he saw and how he got the alto chair in Moody's band
summary: Peter Bailey and Edmund Washington played alto in the band; Washington encouraged him and he replaced Bailey.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: When was the first time you ever saw anybody with a sax? Do you remember?

Yeah, of course I played with the first guy I know was playing alto was Peter Bailey. His son is a bass player now. Chuck. Chuck. His daddy was playing in the same band that I was with Moje. Then we had another guy, he was an Alabama alto player too, Edmund Washington. Big fat dude. Those two who worked in the band were. I haven't seen him watch in a long time. He lived uptown in some way. Yeah. I'd see him up around Carrollton and play when I ran into him on the street. He didn't even know me.
That's the guy who gave me a kind of encouragement. Because Pete used to tell him all the time, oh man, you'll never make a saxophone player.

You'll just hear to see me get on that instrument. And the voice to tell him all the time, go ahead and sound nice. But Washington would tell me all the time, go ahead, you sound nice. And well, when doing rehearsal with the band, I'd take my own with the band, play numbers with the band. So after a while, they got rid of Pete, and they put me in the band, alto.
Which kind of sax was Washington playing?
